method: Independent Haiku judges (general-purpose subagent, model=haiku), one per query, each shown ONLY the 34-skill name+description listing + the single query, asked for the one winning skill. Read-only; no run_loop.py/run_eval.py. METHODOLOGY CHANGE vs all prior runs: the listing is now generated with `skillOverrides` from .claude/settings.json APPLIED, so the 10 tier-2 skills appear as a BARE NAME with no description — that is what the real routing decision sees after the two-tier change. Listing shrinks 32076 -> 24165 chars (-25%) as a side effect.
note: Validation of the 2026-07-28 two-tier routing change: new tier-1 parent `rocq-implementation` created; 10 skills demoted to `name-only` (bv-pitfalls, rocq-pitfalls, iris-proofmode, core-executor-internals, relval-model, relval-rewrite-over-secrets, cfgver-rsolve, cfgver-wp2, cfgver-gen-contract-internals, cfgver-endtoend-internals). Scoped run, not a full sweep: 8 flavour samples (one per demoted child, checking the parent picks up each query flavour) + 9 peer-regression queries (checking the deliberately pushy parent does NOT steal from tier-1 peers). CONCLUSIONS: (1) name-only DOES remove a child from routing competition — no read-confirmed judge ever selected a name-only skill. (2) ZERO peer regressions — the parent stole nothing from any tier-1 skill. (3) The parent UNDER-triggers on conceptual/locational queries: 'what does NonSyncVal represent', 'where do the core monad's refinement lemmas live', and an iApply-failure query all returned `none`, because the description is scoped to WRITING/REPAIRING a proof script and does not claim 'understand or locate something you hit while proving'. That is the single-point-of-failure risk of tiering, materialised, and it needs a targeted description addition + a re-run of Q21/Q73/Q83 before this change can be called done.
harness_caveat: IMPORTANT for anyone reading the raw verdicts: 8 of the first 17 judges returned with tool_uses=0, i.e. they never opened the listing file and answered from guesswork. Haiku is good enough at guessing plausible kebab-case skill names that 5 of those 8 produced real, exactly-spelled skill names (rocq-pitfalls, iris-proofmode, cfgver-wp2, cfgver-gen-contract-internals, core-executor-internals) — all of them demoted skills, which would have looked like 'name-only failed to suppress the child'. Three forced-read controls (prompt requires the Read tool and requires echoing the entry count; all three returned TOTAL=34) flipped two of those verdicts to `none` and one to `rocq-implementation`, proving the demoted-skill answers were hallucinations. LESSON FOR FUTURE RUNS: always require the judge to echo a checksum of the listing (entry count) so a skipped read is detectable; a verdict with tool_uses=0 and no checksum is worthless.

round2.verdict: The two-tier change is sound and the description fix worked: 3 of 3 tiering-caused failures now pass, and 3 of 3 steal guards stayed clean, so widening the parent cost no tier-1 peer. Two residuals, neither blocking: Q21 (a bare name can still out-compete a description on an exact jargon match) and Q44 (a pre-existing rocq-timeout-triage over-trigger).
round2.cost_postmortem: 28 judges at ~30k each, ~850k total — far too expensive for the signal obtained, and ~330k of it was spent unmasking a self-inflicted bug: judges were handed a file PATH rather than an inlined listing, contrary to this skill's own 'ENTIRE input is that listing plus the query' spec, so some skipped the read and hallucinated plausible skill names. Fixes landed the same day: a dedicated `routing-judge` agent (.claude/agents/routing-judge.md, minimal tools, mandatory TOTAL= checksum) and an expanded step 2 in the skill covering inlining, the checksum, the per-judge cost floor, and the scope-before-you-spend arithmetic.
